entries.statement: The DeclaredOnly-then-FlattenHierarchy lookup does not fix the AmbiguousMatchException it targets, and introduces silent misresolution. Three components, per the reverting maintainer: (a) FlattenHierarchy does not flatten INSTANCE members, so a property hidden at an intermediate base type still throws; (b) it silently drops validation attributes depending on which hierarchy level resolves, with no diagnostic — where the original threw loudly; and (c) it adds a third property-resolution policy inconsistent with PropertyHelper.GetVisibleProperties and Microsoft.Extensions.Validation's TryFindProperty.
entries.locus: lines 272-281 at this checkpoint: the DeclaredOnly call followed by `if (propertyInfo is null)` and the FlattenHierarchy retry
entries.source_ref: https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/67712 — revert, merged 2026-07-10, one day after #67075. Body states all three components verbatim; this key entry is quoted from the maintainer's stated reason for reverting.
entries.admission_evidence: Present at checkpoint. Verified in the fixture: DeclaredOnly and FlattenHierarchy each occur once in EditContextDataAnnotationsExtensions.cs. NOT present in this shape at any earlier head — FlattenHierarchy first appears at the final head; earlier heads use a catch(AmbiguousMatchException) retry with DeclaredOnly|IgnoreCase.
entries.must_flag: Flags ANY of the three components: (a) the fallback still throws for intermediate-base hiding (FlattenHierarchy is a no-op for instance members); (b) validation attributes are silently dropped depending on which level resolves, replacing a loud exception with silent misbehavior; (c) it introduces a resolution policy inconsistent with the framework's existing property-resolution helpers. Component (b) is the one that makes this a REGRESSION rather than an incomplete fix — a reviewer that finds only (a) and dismisses it as pre-existing has NOT caught the defect.
